tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

`add()` and `set()` mutate the fragment and return it.

## Initial fragment parsing

Absent and explicitly empty fragments are indistinguishable:

```sh
/workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a 'https://example.com' --b 'B' --c 'C' --d 'D'
```

Exact stdout; first line is empty:

```text

C
D?value
https://example.com#D?value
```

`--a 'https://example.com#'` produces identical output.

A present path fragment:

```sh
/workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a 'https://example.com#old' --b 'B' --c 'C' --d 'D'
```

```text
old
old/C
D?value
https://example.com#D?value
```

The inferred initial parsing heuristic is:

- No `?`:
  - if the fragment contains `=`, the whole fragment is query-only;
  - otherwise it is path-only.
- First `?` splits candidate path/query.
- The right side is treated as query only if it contains `=`.
- Otherwise the entire fragment, including `?`, is path-only.

Examples:

```text
#a/b?x=1&y=2     -> path a/b, query x=1&y=2
#a/b?x           -> path a/b?x, no query
#x=1             -> query x=1, empty path
#?x=1            -> query x=1, empty path; serializes as x=1
#a=b=c           -> query a=b%3Dc
#p?x=1?y=2       -> path p, query x=1%3Fy%3D2
#a??b            -> path a??b, no query
```

A query-order probe:

```sh
/workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a 'https://example.com#p?b=2&a=1&b=3' --b B --c C --d D
```

```text
p?b=2&a=1&b=3
p/C?b=2&a=1&b=3
D?value
https://example.com#D?value
```

Ordering, duplicate keys, repeated `&&`, and empty values are preserved. Example input `#p?a=1&&b=&c` remains `p?a=1&&b=&c`.

## `add(c)` path composition

`c` is always added to the fragment **path**. It is not parsed as a new fragment query. An existing fragment query remains after the path.

Examples:

```text
old       + C        -> old/C
old       + ''       -> old
old       + /        -> old/
old       + //       -> old//
old       + /a//b/   -> old/a//b/
old/      + a        -> old/a
old/      + /a       -> old//a
empty     + /a       -> /a
/         + a        -> /a
/         + /a       -> /a
```

Repeated interior slashes are preserved. Boundary joining is literal segment-based, not simple normalization: notably `old/` plus `/a` gives `old//a`.

With an existing query:

```sh
/workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a 'https://example.com#old?orig=1' --b B --c '?q=2' --d D
```

```text
old?orig=1
old/%3Fq=2?orig=1
D?value
https://example.com#D?value
```

Thus `?q=2` became path text; `orig=1` remained the real query.

If there is no existing query, `%3F` in the path is rendered back as a literal `?`:

```text
old + ?q=1   -> old/?q=1
old + a??b   -> old/a??b
```

With a nonempty existing query, those path question marks remain percent-encoded:

```text
old?orig=1 + ?q=2 -> old/%3Fq=2?orig=1
old?orig=1 + a??b -> old/a%3F%3Fb?orig=1
```

Path `&` and `=` are left raw:

```text
old + a&b     -> old/a&b
old + a=b=c   -> old/a=b=c
```

## `set(d, 'value')`

The positional signature is effectively:

```python
fragment.set(path=d, args='value')
```

It is **not** constructing `d=value`. It:

1. replaces the entire existing path with `d`;
2. replaces the entire existing query with `value`;
3. serializes path first, then `?`, then `value` when both are nonempty.

Therefore initial fragment and `c` are completely discarded by this call.

```sh
/workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a 'https://example.com/base?q=1#old?orig=1' --b B --c C --d 'D'
```

```text
old?orig=1
old/C?orig=1
D?value
https://example.com/base?q=1#D?value
```

The base URL query `?q=1` is preserved separately before `#`.

Special `d` results:

```text
d=''        -> value                  -> #value
d='/'       -> /?value                -> #/?value
d='/a//b/'  -> /a//b/?value
d='?'       -> %3F?value
d='?q=2'    -> %3Fq=2?value
d='a&b'     -> a&b?value
d='a=b=c'   -> a=b=c?value
d='a??b'    -> a%3F%3Fb?value
d='#frag'   -> %23frag?value
```

Because the final query is always nonempty, question marks inside `d` remain encoded as `%3F`.

## Encoding rules observed

Path values, including `c` and `d`:

```text
space       -> %20
é           -> %C3%A9
中          -> %E4%B8%AD
"           -> %22
#           -> %23
bare %      -> %25
%%          -> %25%25
%2f         -> %2F
%c3%a9      -> %C3%A9
%2F         -> %2F, not converted into another path slash
'           -> remains raw
&           -> remains raw
=           -> remains raw
+           -> remains raw
```

Path example:

```text
a%20b/%2F/%%/%25 -> a%20b/%2F/%25%25/%25
a'b"c            -> a'b%22c
é/中             -> %C3%A9/%E4%B8%AD
```

Initial/query-side encoding differs:

```text
space           -> +
Unicode         -> UTF-8 percent escapes
'               -> %27
"               -> %22
extra = in value -> %3D
? inside query  -> %3F
; inside query  -> %3B
```

Examples:

```text
#p?a=hello world&b=café -> p?a=hello+world&b=caf%C3%A9
#p?a="double"&b='single' -> p?a=%22double%22&b=%27single%27
#p?a=x=y=z -> p?a=x%3Dy%3Dz
#p?a=100%25&b=%% -> p?a=100%25&b=%25%25
```
